# Adjudication Task — Chapter 195

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃195화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|원단 첫날 열린 연회는 대성공이라는 말로도 부족했다.
  6|
  7|진위경은 항산검문을 포용함으로써 수십 개 중소 문파의 충성을 받아 내는 파격적인 행보를 보여 줬고, 종남파의 개입과 이미 죽은 줄만 알았던 화왕 적천강의 등장은 모두를 충격에 빠트렸다.
  8|
  9|그리고…….
 10|
 11|‘그중에는 나도 있지.’
 12|
 13|먹고, 마시고, 걸음을 옮기고. 내 일거수일투족마다 사람들의 시선이 따라붙는다.
 14|
 15|반나절 전만 하더라도 그 시선들이 뜻하는 것은 ‘산서잠룡’에 대한 관심이었지만 이제는 아니었다.
 16|
 17|‘화왕의 제자. 열화문의 계승자.’
 18|
 19|곳곳에서 그런 말들이 흘러나오고 있었다. 열화문의 당대 문주인 적천강이 내게 문파의 신물을 넘긴 의미에 대해서, 종남파를 적대하면서까지 태원진가를 보호한 이유에 대해서 쉴 새 없이 떠들고 있다.
 20|
 21|‘이거 어째 반쯤 사실로 굳혀진 것 같은데.’
 22|
 23|사실 나도 적천강의 의중을 잘 모르겠다. 그래서 이 자리에 있는 거고.
 24|
 25|사람들이 정신없는 틈을 타 슬쩍 빠져나온 지금이 바로 적기다.
 26|
 27|“후우.”
 28|
 29|크게 심호흡했다.
 30|
 31|지금 내가 서 있는 곳은 적천강이 머물게 된 처소 앞이었다. 커다란 전각 근처에는 따로 명령이 내려졌는지 쥐 새끼 한 마리 얼씬거리지 않았다.
 32|
 33|“적 대협. 계십니까?”
 34|
 35|문 너머로 대답이 들려왔다.
 36|
 37|“잔다.”
 38|
 39|“여쭤볼 게 있어서 왔습니다.”
 40|
 41|“잔다고.”
 42|
 43|“……주무시는데 대답은 어떻게 하세요?”
 44|
 45|“몽유병이니라.”
 46|
 47|이게 말이여, 망아지여.
 48|
 49|어이가 없었지만 화왕이 그렇다면 그런 거다. 나는 멘탈을 수습하고 다시 입을 열었다.
 50|
 51|“저기, 아무리 생각해도 궁금한 게 있어서 말입니다.”
 52|
 53|“노부가 네 녀석 궁금증 해결해 주는 사람이냐?”
 54|
 55|“그건 아닌데요.”
 56|
 57|“잘 알고 있으면 가서 발 닦고 잠이나 자거라.”
 58|
 59|철벽 보소. 하지만 여기서 물러설 수는 없다.
 60|
 61|굳게 닫힌 문을 향해 아주 조심스럽게, 살금살금 다가가던 그때였다.
 62|
 63|“한 걸음만 더 내디디면 내일 뜨는 해를 못 볼 줄 알아라.”
 64|
 65|“……어떻게 아셨어요?”
 66|
 67|“네놈 인기척이나 천둥소리나 노부에게는 매한가지니까.”
 68|
 69|“그러지 마시고 이제 들여보내 주시면 안 됩니까? 아직 겨울이라 날씨도 쌀쌀한데.”
 70|
 71|“화염신장으로 뜨끈하게 덥혀 주랴?”
 72|
 73|“…….”
 74|
 75|거, 듣는 것만으로도 오장육부가 뜨끈해지네.
 76|
 77|내가 입을 다물자 침묵이 흘렀다. 한동안 이어지던 고요를 깨트린 것은 적천강의 한마디였다.
 78|
 79|“정양(定襄)에 다녀왔다.”
 80|
 81|“아.”
 82|
 83|보잘것없는 구슬 하나에도 누군가에게는 남다른 의미가 있는 법. 정양이 바로 그렇다.
 84|
 85|산서성에 존재하는 수십 개 현읍 중 하나에 불과한 정양의 어느 산길에, 적천강은 가야 할 이유가 있었다.
 86|
 87|‘조필.’
 88|
 89|하늘이 눈을 펑펑 쏟아 내던 그날, 장천으로 살던 한 사내가 조필이라는 이름으로 죽었다.
 90|
 91|“네게 들은 그 자리에서 한참을 머물렀다. 웬 노인이 산기슭을 서성거리니 지나가던 이들이 묻더구나. 왜 여기 있느냐고.”
 92|
 93|가라앉은 목소리가 이어졌다.
 94|
 95|“바로 이곳에서 피붙이가 죽었다고 대답했다. 남은 시신이라도 수습해 주고 싶어서 왔노라고.”
 96|
 97|“…….”
 98|
 99|“그때 깨달았다. 너보다 앞서 그 아이를 만났더라도 결코 죽이지 못했을 거라는 것을. 다시 놓아주고 후회했으리라는 것을 말이다.”
100|
101|문 너머 적천강이 어떤 표정을 짓고 있을지 쉽게 짐작이 가질 않았다.
102|
103|나는 망설이다 입을 열었다.
104|
105|“시신은 찾았습니까?”
106|
107|“아무것도 없었다.”
108|
109|벌써 몇 달이 흘렀다.
110|
111|지금까지 혈로(血路)만 걸어온 인생. 시신을 수습해 줄 수하들도 함께 죽었으니 변덕스러운 날씨에 파묻혔거나, 굶주린 짐승들의 먹이가 되었을 것이다.
112|
113|“늙은이의 욕심이다. 추하고 부질없는.”
114|
115|쪼르륵.
116|
117|술잔을 채우는 소리가 유난히 크게 들렸다.
118|
119|“아까는 취하셨다면서요?”
120|
121|“영악한 놈. 다 알면서 묻기는.”
122|
123|전각 안을 환하게 메운 촛불이 그의 인영을 비춘다.
124|
125|피식, 소리 내어 웃음을 흘린 적천강이 술잔을 꺾었다.
126|
127|“크. 좋다.”
128|
129|한 잔 술에 시름을 털어 버린 듯 후련한 목소리다.
130|
131|문득 적천강이 조필이 죽은 자리를 찾아간 것은, 아직 그를 붙잡고 있는 후회와 미련을 떨쳐 내기 위해서였을 거라는 생각이 들었다.
132|
133|나는 애써 밝은 목소리로 말했다.
134|
135|“좋은 건 나눠야 한다고 배웠습니다만.”
136|
137|“난 어릴 때부터 남의 것을 탐하는 놈은 화염신장으로 지져 버려야 한다고 배웠다.”
138|
139|“어느 무시무시한 분이 그런 말을 했습니까?”
140|
141|“내 스승님.”
142|
143|역시 볼케이노문이야. 가차 없지.
144|
145|어떤 놈이건 간에 화염신장으로 죄다 지져 버리는구나.
146|
147|열화문의 역사와 역대 문주가 누구인지는 모르지만 적천강을 보고 있자면 얼추 짐작이 간다.
148|
149|‘역사 깊은 깡패 문파.’
150|
151|콩 심은 데 콩 나고 팥 심은 데 팥 난다고 했다.
152|
153|그 스승에 그 제자지 뭐. 물론 조필의 경우는 예외지만.
154|
155|‘그나저나 이런 얘기를 하러 온 게 아닌데.’
156|
157|말없이 술만 홀짝거리는 인영을 바라보며 눈치를 살피던 그때. 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.
158|
159|“앞으로 화천검(火天劍)은 네 것이다.”
160|
161|“화, 뭐요?”
162|
163|“화천검. 네 녀석에게 맡긴 검 말이다.”
164|
165|[이름 없는 검]의 진짜 이름을 알게 됐지만 지금 그게 문제가 아니다. 나는 놀라서 말까지 더듬었다.
166|
167|“하, 하지만 이건 열화문의 신물이잖아요.”
168|
169|“아, 신물.”
170|
171|몇 잔째인지 모를 술잔을 기울인 적천강이 말을 이었다.
172|
173|“그거 거짓말이다.”
174|
175|“예?”
176|
177|“신물 아니라고. 백 년 전쯤인가, 본문의 문주였던 어느 분이 쓰시던 걸 후대가 물려받은 거지. 오래되긴 했지만 뭐, 당시에도 신병이기(神兵利器)라 불릴 정도였으니 아직 쓸 만할 게다.”
178|
179|“……!”
180|
181|아니, 이게 무슨 개소리야.
182|
183|나는 생각지도 못한 충격적인 진실에 입을 딱 벌렸다.
184|
185|“그게 다 거짓말이었다고요? 지금 저 놀리시는 거죠?”
186|
187|“놀려? 너 같은 핏덩이를 뭣 하러?”
188|
189|“사람들 앞에서 그러셨잖아요! 저놈에게 열화문의 신물을 맡겼다!”
190|
191|“그랬지. 사람들 앞이니까.”
192|
193|적천강이 심드렁한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
194|
195|“그 정도는 해 줘야 세인들이 떠들 것 아니냐. 아, 저놈이 화왕과 깊은 연관이 있구나. 신물을 맡겼으니 제자가 아닐까. 태원진가를 건드리면 그 무시무시한 화왕이 나서겠구나. 뭐 그런 소문이 일파만파 퍼지겠지.”
196|
197|“…….”
198|
199|“설마 노부가 네 녀석 같은 애송이한테 본문의 신물을 맡기겠느냐? 어차피 일인전승이라 아는 사람도 없는데 내가 신물이라고 하면 그게 신물인 거지.”
200|
201|“…….”
202|
203|“그러니 검은 계속 갖고 있어라. 그래야 종남파 놈들이 감히 나서지 못할 테니.”
204|
205|이거 꿈인가. 충격에 빠진 내 귓가로 확인 사살을 알리는 시스템 알림이 울렸다.
206|
207|띠링.
208|
209|
210|
211|- [이름 없는 검]에 관한 정보가 갱신되었습니다.
212|
213|
214|
215|아이템창
216|
217|
218|
219|[화천검]
220|
221|종류 : 검
222|
223|등급 : 절정
224|
225|제한 : [열화문]의 진전을 이은 자
226|
227|설명 : 열화문의 십 대 문주가 사용하던 애검. 만년한철로 제작되어 매우 날카롭고 단단하다. 오랜 세월 수많은 주인을 거치며 스스로 변화했다. 열화문의 진전을 이은 자만이 진정한 힘을 끌어낼 수 있다.
228|
229|효과 : 알 수 없음
230|
231|
232|
233|
234|
235|갱신된 정보는 적천강의 말 그대로였다. 십 대 문주가 사용하던 애검. 열화문의 신물이라는 말은 눈 씻고 찾아봐도 없다.
236|
237|그나마 검에 숨겨져 있다는 ‘진정한 힘’조차도 열화문의 진전을 이어야 한단다.
238|
239|한마디로 만년한철인 것을 빼면 시체라는 뜻.
240|
241|‘난 진짜 신물인 줄 알았는데. 열화문의 제자로 삼겠다고 하면 어쩌나 엄청 고민했는데…….’
242|
243|허탈하게 홀로그램 창을 바라보는 내게 적천강이 선심 쓰는 듯 덧붙였다.
244|
245|“장기 대여라고 생각해라. 노부가 깜빡하고 그대로 죽어 버리면 가져도 좋다. 아, 화염신장의 비급은 지금 당장 뱉어 내고.”
246|
247|“망할 늙은이…… 헉.”
248|
249|생각만 한다는 게 그만 입 밖으로 튀어나와 버렸다.
250|
251|화들짝 놀라 입을 다문 그 순간, 굳게 닫혀 있던 전각의 문이 그대로 터져 나갔다.
252|
253|우지직!
254|
255|화염이 이글거리는 한 쌍의 눈동자가 날 응시했다.
256|
257|“이 핏덩이 같은 놈이. 방금 뭐라 했느냐?”
258|
259|“마, 마, 말실수였는데요.”
260|
261|“말실수? 그럼 노부도 손 실수 한 번 하마.”
262|
263|후욱!
264|
265|붉게 달아오른 손바닥과 압도적인 열기.
266|
267|나는 뒤도 돌아보지 않고 몸을 돌렸다. 찰나의 순간 인벤토리에서 꺼낸 화염신장의 비급을 던지는 것도 잊지 않았다.
268|
269|“헉, 비급, 화염신장의 비급이!”
270|
271|그대로 손을 뻗었다가는 비급이 잿가루가 될 판.
272|
273|대경한 적천강이 황급히 주먹을 거둬들인다. 나는 그 틈을 타 죽을힘을 다해 뛰었다.
274|
275|“죄송합니다! 진짜 죄송해요! 살려 주세요!”
276|
277|“이, 이 죽일 놈! 거기 안 서!”
278|
279|등 뒤로 그의 고함이 쩌렁쩌렁 울렸다.
280|
281|
282|
283|* * *
284|
285|
286|
287|꽁지가 빠지도록 도망가는 진태경의 뒷모습을 바라보던 적천강이 피식 웃었다.
288|
289|방금 전까지 얼굴에 가득하던 분노의 기색은 씻은 듯이 사라진 후였다.
290|
291|“이놈아, 네가 아무리 도망쳐 봐야 노부의 손바닥 안이니라.”
292|
293|잡으려 한다면 얼마든지 잡을 수 있다.
294|
295|그러나 적천강은 뒷짐을 지고 돌아섰다.
296|
297|자식처럼 아끼던 제자, 장천을 죽인 장본인이지만 진태경에 대한 증오는 없다. 오히려 적천강이 진심으로 사과해야 할 사람 중 하나다.
298|
299|이 모든 것은 십 년 전, 그의 잘못된 선택으로부터 비롯되었으니까.
300|
301|“망할 늙은이라고 했지.”
302|
303|핏덩이 같은 어린놈에게 폭언을 들었음에도 기분이 나쁘지 않았다. 아니, 오히려 후련하기까지 했다.
304|
305|“그렇지. 나야 말로 망할 늙은이고 노망난 늙은이지. 허허, 허허허.”
306|
307|스승이 죽은 이후, 감히 어느 누구도 적천강의 면전에서 그를 비난하거나 욕하지 못했다.
308|
309|그는 화왕이니까. 홀로 전설을 써 내려간 위대한 무인이니까.
310|
311|그러던 차에 진태경의 한마디를 들으니 오랫동안 막혀 있던 뭔가가 뻥 뚫린 기분이다.
312|
313|“시원하군. 시원해.”
314|

I didn’t know the history of the Fire Gate Clan or the names of its past Sect Leaders, but looking at Jeok Cheongang gave me a pretty good idea.

[P76]
*An ancient sect of thugs.*

[P77]
They said beans grew where beans were planted and red beans where red beans were planted.

[P78]
Like master, like disciple. Jopil was the exception, of course.

[P79]
*Anyway, this isn’t what I came here to talk about.*

[P80]
I was watching the silent silhouette sip his liquor and trying to gauge his mood when Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke.

[P81]
“From now on, the Fire Heaven Sword is yours.”

[P82]
“Fire… what?”

[P83]
“The Fire Heaven Sword. The sword I entrusted to you.”

[P84]
I had just learned the Unnamed Sword’s true name, but that wasn’t the issue right now. I was so shocked that I stammered.

[P85]
“B-but that’s the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.”

[P86]
“Ah, the sacred treasure.”

[P87]
Jeok Cheongang tipped back yet another cup of liquor before continuing.

[P88]
“That was a lie.”

[P89]
“What?”

[P90]
“It isn’t a sacred treasure. One of our sect’s Sect Leaders used it about a hundred years ago, and later generations inherited it from him. It’s old, but it was already renowned as a divine weapon back then, so it should still be useful.”

[P91]
“…!”

[P92]
What the hell was he talking about?

[P93]
I stood there with my mouth hanging open at the shocking revelation.

[P94]
“That was all a lie? You’re messing with me, right?”

[P95]
“Messing with you? Why would I bother with a little pup like you?”

[P96]
“You said it in front of everyone! ‘I entrusted that boy with the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure!’”

[P97]
“I did. Because everyone was there.”

[P98]
Jeok Cheongang continued in an indifferent voice.

[P99]
“I had to go that far to get people talking. ‘That boy must have a deep connection to the Fire King. Perhaps he is the Fire King’s Disciple, since he was entrusted with the sacred treasure. If anyone touches the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that terrifying Fire King will step in.’ Rumors like that will spread far and wide.”

[P100]
“…”

[P101]
“Do you really think this old man would entrust our sect’s sacred treasure to a young brat like you? Our arts are passed down to only one successor per generation, so no one else knows the truth. If I say it is a sacred treasure, then it is a sacred treasure.”

[P102]
“…”

[P103]
“So keep the sword. That way, those Zhongnan bastards won’t dare make a move.”

[P104]
*Is this a dream?*

[P105]
As I stood there in shock, a System notification rang in my ears, delivering the final blow.

[P106]
Ding.

[P107]
> **System**
>
> Information regarding the Unnamed Sword has been updated.
>
> **Item Window**
>
> **Fire Heaven Sword**
>
> **Type:** Sword  
> **Grade:** Peak  
> **Restriction:** One who has inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy  
> **Description:** The beloved sword once used by the Fire Gate Clan’s tenth Sect Leader. Forged from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, it is exceptionally sharp and durable. After passing through the hands of countless owners over many years, it changed of its own accord. Only one who has inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy can draw out its true power.
>
> **Effect:** Unknown

[P108]
The updated information was exactly as Jeok Cheongang had said.

[P109]
It was the beloved sword of the tenth Sect Leader. No matter how hard I looked, there wasn’t a single mention of it being the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.

[P110]
Even the “true power” hidden within the sword could only be drawn out by someone who had inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy.

[P111]
In other words, other than the fact that it was made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, the sword was a corpse.

[P112]
*I really thought it was a sacred treasure. I spent so much time worrying about what I’d do if he said he wanted to make me his Disciple…*

[P113]
As I stared blankly at the holographic window, Jeok Cheongang added as though he were doing me a great favor.

[P114]
“Think of it as a long-term loan. If this old man forgets about it and dies, you may keep it. Ah, and hand over the Flame Divine Palm manual right now.”

[P115]
“Damn old man… Gasp.”

[P116]
I had only meant to think it, but the words slipped out of my mouth.

[P117]
I clapped my mouth shut in alarm. At that very moment, the firmly closed pavilion door burst outward.

[P118]
Crack!

[P119]
A pair of eyes blazing with fire glared at me.

[P120]
“You little pup. What did you just say?”

[P121]
“I-I-I misspoke.”

[P122]
“Misspoke? Then this old man will make a little mistake with his hand, too.”

[P123]
Whoosh!

[P124]
A palm glowed red-hot, radiating overwhelming heat.

[P125]
I spun around without looking back. In the same instant, I pulled the Flame Divine Palm manual from my Inventory and threw it.

[P126]
“Gasp! The manual! The Flame Divine Palm manual!”

[P127]
If he reached out now, the manual would turn to ash.

[P128]
Jeok Cheongang recoiled in alarm and hastily pulled back his fist. I seized the opening and ran for my life.

[P129]
“I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! Please spare me!”

[P130]
“You damned bastard! Stop right there!”

[P131]
His roar thundered behind me.

[P132]
* * *

[P133]
Jeok Cheongang watched Jin Taekyung flee as though his tail were on fire and let out a quiet laugh.

[P134]
The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.

[P135]
“You little fool. No matter how far you run, you are still in the palm of this old man’s hand.”

[P136]
He could catch Taekyung whenever he wished.

[P137]
But Jeok Cheongang merely clasped his hands behind his back and turned away.

[P138]
Jin Taekyung had killed Jangcheon, the Disciple Jeok Cheongang had cherished like a son.

[P139]
Yet Jeok Cheongang bore him no hatred.

[P140]
If anything, Taekyung was one of the people to whom Jeok Cheongang owed a sincere apology.

[P141]
Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.

[P142]
“He called me a damn old man.”

[P143]
Despite being cursed by a little pup, Jeok Cheongang wasn’t offended.

[P144]
No, if anything, he felt relieved.

[P145]
“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old fool, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

[P146]
After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.

[P147]
He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.

[P148]
Yet hearing those words from Jin Taekyung made him feel as though something that had been blocked for years had finally burst open.

[P149]
“How refreshing. Truly refreshing.”

[P150]
As people grew older, they became lonelier by the day. Not because they had no one beside them, but because they had no one to lean on.

[P151]
Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.

[P152]
“To be someone’s support…”

[P153]
Jeok Cheongang was a rough, sharp thorn tree. He had lived a long life and crossed paths with countless people, but he had never allowed anyone to lean on him.

[P154]
There had been only one exception.

[P155]
Jangcheon.

[P156]
“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”

[P157]
As Jeok Cheongang thought of him, his gaze clouded over. But his chest no longer hurt as much as it once had, nor did his eyes grow hot.

[P158]
The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.

[P159]
At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.

[P160]
He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.

[P161]
“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”

[P162]
If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.

[P163]
He might still think of his dead Disciple from time to time. But those thoughts would no longer be regrets about the past.

[P164]
They would be memories.

[P165]
“This is enough. This is how it should be.”

[P166]
After pacing around the courtyard for a long while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly stopped.

[P167]
Jangcheon’s face vanished from before his eyes, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.

[P168]
*Why him?*

[P169]
Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.

[P170]
The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.

[P171]
*Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?*

[P172]
Jeok Cheongang frowned.

[P173]
Sizzle.

[P174]
Something began to burn, sending up a thin trail of smoke.

[P175]
Realizing where the sound had come from, his eyes flew open.

[P176]
“The manual!”

[P177]
The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual had already burned halfway through.

[P178]
Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

[P179]
“Jin Taekyung! You bastard! I’ll kill you!”

“I had to go that far to get people talking. ‘That boy must have a deep connection to the Fire King. Perhaps he is the Fire King’s Disciple, since he was entrusted with the sacred treasure. If anyone touches the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that terrifying Fire King will step in.’ Rumors like that will spread far and wide.”

[P100]
“…”

[P101]
“Do you really think this old man would entrust our sect’s sacred treasure to a young brat like you? Our arts are passed down to only one successor per generation, so no one else knows the truth. If I say it is a sacred treasure, then it is a sacred treasure.”

[P102]
“…”

[P103]
“So keep the sword. That way, those Zhongnan bastards won’t dare make a move.”

[P104]
*Is this a dream?*

[P105]
As I stood there in shock, a System notification rang in my ears, delivering the final blow.

[P106]
Ding.

[P107]
> **System**
>
> Information regarding the Unnamed Sword has been updated.
>
> **Item Window**
>
> **Fire Heaven Sword**
>
> **Type:** Sword  
> **Grade:** Peak  
> **Restriction:** One who has inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy  
> **Description:** The beloved sword once used by the Fire Gate Clan’s tenth Sect Leader. Forged from Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, it is exceptionally sharp and durable. After passing through the hands of countless owners over many years, it changed of its own accord. Only one who has inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy can draw out its true power.
>
> **Effect:** Unknown

[P108]
The updated information was exactly as Jeok Cheongang had said.

[P109]
It was the beloved sword of the tenth Sect Leader. No matter how hard I looked, there wasn’t a single mention of it being the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.

[P110]
Even the “true power” hidden within the sword could only be drawn out by someone who had inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy.

[P111]
In other words, other than the fact that it was made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, the sword was a corpse.

[P112]
*I really thought it was a sacred treasure. I spent so much time worrying about what I’d do if he said he wanted to make me his Disciple…*

[P113]
As I stared blankly at the holographic window, Jeok Cheongang added as though he were doing me a great favor.

[P114]
“Think of it as a long-term loan. If this old man forgets about it and dies, you may keep it. Ah, and hand over the Flame Divine Palm manual right now.”

[P115]
“Damn old man… Gasp.”

[P116]
I had only meant to think it, but the words slipped out of my mouth.

[P117]
I clapped my mouth shut in alarm. At that very moment, the firmly closed pavilion door burst outward.

[P118]
Crack!

[P119]
A pair of eyes blazing with fire glared at me.

[P120]
“You little pup. What did you just say?”

[P121]
“I-I-I misspoke.”

[P122]
“Misspoke? Then this old man will make a little mistake with his hand, too.”

[P123]
Whoosh!

[P124]
A palm glowed red-hot, radiating overwhelming heat.

[P125]
I spun around without looking back. In the same instant, I pulled the Flame Divine Palm manual from my Inventory and threw it.

[P126]
“Gasp! The manual! The Flame Divine Palm manual!”

[P127]
If he reached out now, the manual would turn to ash.

[P128]
Jeok Cheongang recoiled in alarm and hastily pulled back his fist. I seized the opening and ran for my life.

[P129]
“I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! Please spare me!”

[P130]
“You damned bastard! Stop right there!”

[P131]
His roar thundered behind me.

[P132]
* * *

[P133]
Jeok Cheongang watched Jin Taekyung flee as though his tail were on fire and let out a quiet laugh.

[P134]
The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.

[P135]
“You little fool. No matter how far you run, you are still in the palm of this old man’s hand.”

[P136]
He could catch Taekyung whenever he wished.

[P137]
But Jeok Cheongang merely clasped his hands behind his back and turned away.

[P138]
Jin Taekyung had killed Jangcheon, the Disciple Jeok Cheongang had cherished like a son.

[P139]
Yet Jeok Cheongang bore him no hatred.

[P140]
If anything, Taekyung was one of the people to whom Jeok Cheongang owed a sincere apology.

[P141]
Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.

[P142]
“He called me a damn old man.”

[P143]
Despite being cursed by a little pup, Jeok Cheongang wasn’t offended.

[P144]
No, if anything, he felt relieved.

[P145]
“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old fool, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

[P146]
After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.

[P147]
He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.

[P148]
Yet hearing those words from Jin Taekyung made him feel as though something that had been blocked for years had finally burst open.

[P149]
“How refreshing. Truly refreshing.”

[P150]
As people grew older, they became lonelier by the day. Not because they had no one beside them, but because they had no one to lean on.

[P151]
Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.

[P152]
“To be someone’s support…”

[P153]
Jeok Cheongang was a rough, sharp thorn tree. He had lived a long life and crossed paths with countless people, but he had never allowed anyone to lean on him.

[P154]
There had been only one exception.

[P155]
Jangcheon.

[P156]
“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”

[P157]
As Jeok Cheongang thought of him, his gaze clouded over. But his chest no longer hurt as much as it once had, nor did his eyes grow hot.

[P158]
The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.

[P159]
At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.

[P160]
He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.

[P161]
“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”

[P162]
If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.

[P163]
He might still think of his dead Disciple from time to time. But those thoughts would no longer be regrets about the past.

[P164]
They would be memories.

[P165]
“This is enough. This is how it should be.”

[P166]
After pacing around the courtyard for a long while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly stopped.

[P167]
Jangcheon’s face vanished from before his eyes, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.

[P168]
*Why him?*

[P169]
Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.

[P170]
The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.

[P171]
*Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?*

[P172]
Jeok Cheongang frowned.

[P173]
Sizzle.

[P174]
Something began to burn, sending up a thin trail of smoke.

[P175]
Realizing where the sound had come from, his eyes flew open.

[P176]
“The manual!”

[P177]
The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual had already burned halfway through.

[P178]
Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

[P179]
“Jin Taekyung! You bastard! I’ll kill you!”

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. ### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 195

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃195화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|원단 첫날 열린 연회는 대성공이라는 말로도 부족했다.
  6|
  7|진위경은 항산검문을 포용함으로써 수십 개 중소 문파의 충성을 받아 내는 파격적인 행보를 보여 줬고, 종남파의 개입과 이미 죽은 줄만 알았던 화왕 적천강의 등장은 모두를 충격에 빠트렸다.
  8|
  9|그리고…….
 10|
 11|‘그중에는 나도 있지.’
 12|
 13|먹고, 마시고, 걸음을 옮기고. 내 일거수일투족마다 사람들의 시선이 따라붙는다.
 14|
 15|반나절 전만 하더라도 그 시선들이 뜻하는 것은 ‘산서잠룡’에 대한 관심이었지만 이제는 아니었다.
 16|
 17|‘화왕의 제자. 열화문의 계승자.’
 18|
 19|곳곳에서 그런 말들이 흘러나오고 있었다. 열화문의 당대 문주인 적천강이 내게 문파의 신물을 넘긴 의미에 대해서, 종남파를 적대하면서까지 태원진가를 보호한 이유에 대해서 쉴 새 없이 떠들고 있다.
 20|
 21|‘이거 어째 반쯤 사실로 굳혀진 것 같은데.’
 22|
 23|사실 나도 적천강의 의중을 잘 모르겠다. 그래서 이 자리에 있는 거고.
 24|
 25|사람들이 정신없는 틈을 타 슬쩍 빠져나온 지금이 바로 적기다.
 26|
 27|“후우.”
 28|
 29|크게 심호흡했다.
 30|
 31|지금 내가 서 있는 곳은 적천강이 머물게 된 처소 앞이었다. 커다란 전각 근처에는 따로 명령이 내려졌는지 쥐 새끼 한 마리 얼씬거리지 않았다.
 32|
 33|“적 대협. 계십니까?”
 34|
 35|문 너머로 대답이 들려왔다.
 36|
 37|“잔다.”
 38|
 39|“여쭤볼 게 있어서 왔습니다.”
 40|
 41|“잔다고.”
 42|
 43|“……주무시는데 대답은 어떻게 하세요?”
 44|
 45|“몽유병이니라.”
 46|
 47|이게 말이여, 망아지여.
 48|
 49|어이가 없었지만 화왕이 그렇다면 그런 거다. 나는 멘탈을 수습하고 다시 입을 열었다.
 50|
 51|“저기, 아무리 생각해도 궁금한 게 있어서 말입니다.”
 52|
 53|“노부가 네 녀석 궁금증 해결해 주는 사람이냐?”
 54|
 55|“그건 아닌데요.”
 56|
 57|“잘 알고 있으면 가서 발 닦고 잠이나 자거라.”
 58|
 59|철벽 보소. 하지만 여기서 물러설 수는 없다.
 60|

[P149]

Jangcheon.

[P165]

[P132]
* * *

[P133]
Jeok Cheongang watched Jin Taekyung flee as though his tail were on fire and let out a quiet laugh.

[P134]
The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.

[P135]
“You little fool. No matter how far you run, you are still in the palm of this old man’s hand.”

[P136]
He could catch Taekyung whenever he wished.

[P137]
But Jeok Cheongang merely clasped his hands behind his back and turned away.

[P138]
Jin Taekyung had killed Jangcheon, the Disciple Jeok Cheongang had cherished like a son.

[P139]
Yet Jeok Cheongang bore him no hatred.

[P140]
If anything, Taekyung was one of the people to whom Jeok Cheongang owed a sincere apology.

[P141]
Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.

[P142]
“He called me a damn old man.”

[P143]
Despite being cursed by a little pup, Jeok Cheongang wasn’t offended.

[P144]
No, if anything, he felt relieved.

[P145]
“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old fool, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

[P146]
After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.

[P147]
He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.

[P148]
Yet hearing those words from Jin Taekyung made him feel as though something that had been blocked for years had finally burst open.

[P149]
“How refreshing. Truly refreshing.”

[P150]
As people grew older, they became lonelier by the day. Not because they had no one beside them, but because they had no one to lean on.

[P151]
Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.

[P152]
“To be someone’s support…”

[P153]
Jeok Cheongang was a rough, sharp thorn tree. He had lived a long life and crossed paths with countless people, but he had never allowed anyone to lean on him.

[P154]
There had been only one exception.

[P155]
Jangcheon.

[P156]
“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”

[P157]
As Jeok Cheongang thought of him, his gaze clouded over. But his chest no longer hurt as much as it once had, nor did his eyes grow hot.

[P158]
The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.

[P159]
At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.

[P160]
He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.

[P161]
“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”

[P162]
If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.

[P163]
He might still think of his dead Disciple from time to time. But those thoughts would no longer be regrets about the past.

[P164]
They would be memories.

[P165]
“This is enough. This is how it should be.”

[P166]
After pacing around the courtyard for a long while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly stopped.

[P167]
Jangcheon’s face vanished from before his eyes, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.

[P168]
*Why him?*

[P169]
Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.

[P170]
The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.

[P171]
*Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?*

[P172]
Jeok Cheongang frowned.

[P173]
Sizzle.

[P174]
Something began to burn, sending up a thin trail of smoke.

[P175]
Realizing where the sound had come from, his eyes flew open.

[P176]
“The manual!”

[P177]
The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual had already burned halfway through.

[P178]
Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

[P179]
“Jin Taekyung! You bastard! I’ll kill you!”

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
